regime_context: The detector shows a broad, two-horse leadership structure in Canada: Oil & Gas Producers lead decisively (score 2.24, 92.9% breadth, crowded) with Big Banks as the only credentialed challenger (0.85, 85.7% breadth, trending). Half the universe is trend-eligible, the absolute-trend gate has helped historically on this market (drawdown control, not return forecasting), and this desk's own prior directional calls have been poor (dir_accuracy 0.316) — so conviction is capped low.
emerging_watch: Watching whether Big Banks close the leadership margin versus Oil & Gas — a confirmed handoff would need a rotation margin below ~0.5 and banks' breadth holding above 0.8 for 10+ trading days; until then this is a durable follower, not a new leader.

theses.subject: Oil & Gas Producers
theses.thesis: The trend-gate leg (only validated edge) is positive: eligible, durability 0.69, and 92.9% breadth shows participation is broad rather than single-name speculation. Rank leadership reflects where focus is concentrating, not a forecast. The crowding flag (z=1.18) is a size-down caution only, not a fade.
theses.dissent: Oil & Gas is crowded and the theme is already widely owned; energy leadership in Canada is often a late-cycle value trade that mean-reverts sharply on any commodity supply surprise or demand scare.

falsifier.text: XEG.TO breaks below its 50-day moving average while breadth falls below 0.7 before the check-by date

theses.subject: Big Banks
theses.thesis: The only non-energy theme with both trend eligibility and a clean trend tag (hurst=trend, breadth 0.857, durability 0.71). It is the sole credible challenger in the rotation structure but the margin to the leader (1.39) is too wide to call a handoff — so this is a durable second-leg lean, not a rotation bet.
theses.dissent: Canadian banks are rate-spread sensitive and face a concentrated domestic credit cycle; if the macro backdrop shifts toward growth concerns, financials typically lag energy and defensives.

falsifier.text: ZEB.TO lags XEG.TO by 5% over a rolling 20-day window before the check-by date

theses.subject: Technology
theses.thesis: Technically trend-eligible (hurst=trend, durability 0.71) but the score is marginally negative (-0.03) and crowding is elevated (z=1.35) with no supporting breadth edge over peers. The macro narrative is AI_tech-heavy, but that is coincident context, not a trigger — and crowded tech in Canada has historically marked attention peaks, not entries.
theses.dissent: Canada's tech index is narrow and AI-capital-expenditure-driven; if global AI capex guidance accelerates, even a crowded Canadian tech basket can keep trending for quarters.

falsifier.text: XIT.TO outperforms XEG.TO by 3% over a rolling 15-day window before the check-by date

macro_narrative.note: market-level macro/policy/geo narrative flow; coincident, not per-theme, never a trigger
